welcome.title: Welcome to Backchannel
welcome.selectSession: Select a session from the sidebar or create a new one to get started.
welcome.intro: Backchannel works alongside your meetings: it transcribes the call live with speaker attribution, surfaces questions, objections, and opportunities as they happen, and writes a briefing you can review, export, or chat with afterwards.
welcome.chooseModelsBody: Built-in local transcription works without a key. Connect Google, OpenAI, or a self-hosted service if you want its models, then choose a model for each enabled agent. Recommended marks a good starting point.
welcome.firstSessionBody: A session holds everything about one meeting: participants, documents, directives, the transcript, and every insight the agents find.
welcome.startCallTitle: Start the call, or import one
welcome.startCallBody: From the session screen, start live capture (microphone plus optional tab or system audio), or import an existing recording or transcript to run the same analysis after the fact.
welcome.footer: You can tune agents, models, prompts, and privacy at any time under Administration.

privacy.title: Privacy First
privacy.body: Keeps every byte of call audio and transcript on this machine. Transcription switches to local ONNX models, and any feature that needs an outside API call is turned off until the switch is turned back off.
privacy.active: Active: transcription runs on {{model}}. Cloud AI agents, live captions, analysis, chat, and document summarization are off. Your previous cloud model choices are restored when you turn this off.
privacy.review: Review what changes before enabling. These features stop working because they have no local alternative:

modelOptions.endpointOff: - endpoint is not on your machine/LAN, off in {{lock}}

recorder.unsupported: Browser microphone recording is not available.

batchTranscription.title: Batch Transcription
batchTranscription.body: Controls the model used to create saved transcript lines from audio imports and finalized diarized live-call segments.
batchTranscription.languageBody: Tells Whisper, Gemini and OpenAI which language to expect, for both the saved transcript and live captions. They transcribe what is said without translating it. Parakeet takes no language setting: v2 is English-only, and v3 detects which of its 25 European languages is spoken.
batchTranscription.localOnly: {{switch}} is on: only local ONNX models can transcribe. Cloud live-caption gateways are off, but the experimental on-device captioner ({{captioner}}) can be selected here, English-only or multilingual (Parakeet v3 Live) - it is CPU-heavy, so check the fit test's live-caption feasibility first. Your previous cloud choices are restored when the switch is turned off.
batchTranscription.details: Batch transcription runs after audio has been segmented by the diarizer and produces the saved transcript. Live preview is separate: the Audio Bridge agent (Gemini Live or OpenAI Realtime, depending on the model) only shows interim captions while a call is active. Changing the live preview model here updates that agent's model, the same setting shown on the Agents tab. Self-hosted (OpenAI-compatible chat) models are text-only and are not listed here; for fully offline transcription choose a local ONNX model (Whisper Base, or Parakeet v2 for English and Parakeet v3 for 25 European languages), and use a self-hosted chat model for the analysis agents.

localFit.loadFailed: Unable to load local models. The backend may still be starting.
localFit.title: Local Model Fit Test
localFit.body: Times a role-sized call on each local text model and the bundled ASR models, then checks whether each agent keeps up. Speed only, not answer quality.
localFit.noModels: No self-hosted text models found. Add an on-prem OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM) under Connections to test local analysis. The bundled ASR models are still tested below.
localFit.runningBody: Running the fit test... timing each text model and the local ASR models. First run may download the ASR models.
localFit.asrBody: Real-time factor for the bundled speech-to-text models. Run fit test measures them on a synthetic clip (an estimate); upload or record real speech for a precise number. Live-caption feasibility is experimental (see roadmap): a projection of whether a rolling-window local captioner could keep up.
localFit.footer: To run an agent on a local model, also select it on the Agents tab. Budgets you set here are per-model: the agent uses this budget only when it runs that model. Live interim captions have no local option today (they need a cloud streaming model).
localFit.loadDescription: Reserve for recording, diarization, and other apps: {{value}}x measured latency
localFit.briefingNote: Briefing agents run once at call end (no live loop), so they show an acceptable-wait verdict, not a cycle budget.

diarization.enhancedBody: Enhanced uses NeMo Sortformer after this machine passes the benchmark. It can separate speaker turns more accurately in multi-speaker calls, but it is heavier and processes audio in short batches.

coverage.text: Transcripts, insights, briefings, chat and documents
coverage.textOn: Every line is tokenized as it is written, so each model prompt is built from clean text. Cloud text models receive tokens only.
coverage.textOff: Turn the shield on to tokenize new text. Sessions recorded earlier keep what they hold until you protect them.
coverage.audioEnforced: Audio cannot be tokenized, so while the shield is on transcription is held to a local model ({{model}}); cloud transcribers are locked in Transcription & Audio.
coverage.audioLocal: Transcription runs on this machine ({{model}}), so no audio leaves it.
coverage.audioCloud: Call audio goes to {{model}} to be transcribed, and spoken names travel with it. Turn the shield on to hold transcription to a local model.
coverage.gatewayPaused: {{model}} is configured but skipped while the shield is on: a cloud gateway would hear the names the shield withholds. Live captions stay off unless the Audio Bridge uses the on-device captioner.
coverage.gatewayCloud: Live audio streams to {{model}} for interim captions. Switch it to the on-device captioner or disable it in Agents.
coverage.gatewayOff: The audio gateway is off or has no model selected, so no live audio leaves this machine.
coverage.refinementOn: The refiner only ever reads tokenized text, so it stays covered on any model, local or cloud, and a rewrite is kept only if it carries exactly the original tokens. {{status}}
coverage.refinementRunning: Running now on {{model}}, every {{seconds}}s and at call end.
coverage.refinementOff: Currently off; enable the Transcript Refiner in Agents to polish punctuation, casing and misshearings.
coverage.refinementDisabled: Turn the shield on to tokenize new text; until then the refiner reads whatever the transcript holds.

pii.nerInstallFailed: The on-device model could not be installed.
pii.nerBody: A small named-entity model ({{model}}, about 110 MB) finds people, companies and places in free text. It downloads once and then runs offline on the CPU. Without it the shield still catches speaker names, protected terms, introductions, names it has seen before, and every structured identifier.
pii.termsBody: Names the model might miss and that must never leave this machine: client companies, project code names, a person who is never introduced. Matched as whole words in every session.
pii.showPreview: Show what a model would see
pii.previewHint: Nothing is stored; the preview numbers tokens from 1.
pii.noMatches: Nothing in that text matched the enabled categories.
pii.outboundBody: With the log on, every prompt is written to the data directory exactly as it leaves for a model, so you can confirm the models only ever see tokens. While the shield is on, a prompt that still carries a vault value is refused before it is sent and appears here marked blocked.

pii.title: PII Shield
pii.body: Replaces names, contact details and identifiers with tokens such as [PERSON_1] before anything is stored or shown to a model, local or cloud. The real values sit in an encrypted vault on this machine and are put back only on the screen in front of you and in exports you ask for.
